svg.title: Cells
svg.desc: Animal cells: Eukaryotic: DNA enclosed in a nucleus. Nucleus: genes control activities. Cytoplasm: enzyme-controlled reactions. Membrane: controls entry/exit. Mitochondria: aerobic respiration transfers energy. Ribosomes: protein synthesis. Plant cells: Have all the animal-cell structures, plus: Cellulose wall: strength/support; also in algae. Permanent vacuole: cell sap; water keeps the cell firm. Chloroplasts: chlorophyll absorbs light for photosynthesis. Only in photosynthetic cells; normally absent from root hairs. Bacterial cells: Prokaryotic: much smaller; no nucleus. Main DNA loop in cytoplasm; some have plasmids (extra genes). Have membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes and a non-cellulose wall. No mitochondria/chloroplasts. Sperm cells: Tail → swimming. Mitochondria → energy for movement. Acrosome enzymes → penetrate the egg’s outer layers. Nerve & muscle cells: Nerve: long fibre carries impulses; branched ends connect cells. Muscle: contractile proteins shorten the cell; mitochondria supply energy for contraction. Root hair cells: Long extension → large absorption area. Water enters by osmosis. Minerals enter by active transport when less concentrated in soil; mitochondria supply energy. Normally no chloroplasts underground. Xylem & phloem: Xylem: dead, hollow tubes carry water/minerals; lignin strengthens walls against collapse. Phloem: sieve tubes carry dissolved sugars; companion cells supply energy for loading. Explain feature → effect → function, including in unfamiliar cells. Differentiation: Developing specialised structures for a job. Animals: mainly early in development; plants: many cells throughout life. Mature animal cell division mainly repairs/replaces cells. Differentiation is the process; specialisation is the result.
